card.title: PS5 BLOD and 2-second shutdown diagnostic steps

claims.statement: Continuous pulsing blue light indicates the system is continuously running diagnostic checks without completing boot.
claims.evidence: System status LED stays in a pulsing state during startup checks.
claims.quote: Is keeps pulsating because it keeps running checks.

claims.statement: Liquid metal spills beneath the APU or its seals can cause 2-second shutdown or BLOD errors.
claims.evidence: Visual inspection reveals short-circuiting liquid metal contamination in the APU area.
claims.quote: First check liquid metal spills on board and APU. Check APU if metal liquid is under the seals or under the APU.

claims.statement: Failure of the HDMI encoder IC can manifest as a blue light of death or 2-second shutdown.
claims.evidence: HDMI encoder IC fault mode list directly links it to BLOD and 2-second shutdown.
claims.quote: If the Encoder IC fails, you can get • No Picture • No Power • blue light of death • Also 2 seconds of death

claims.statement: If all power rails are present and no shorts are found during BLOD troubleshooting, APU or RAM BGA failure is likely.
claims.evidence: Absence of power rail shorts with proper rail voltages points to BGA IC fault.
claims.quote: If all power rails are present and no shorts found, then it can be a BGA IC problem. Most likely it is APU / RAM problem.

claims.statement: A single beep repeating every 5 to 10 seconds when pressing the power button can indicate a short circuit.
claims.evidence: Beep feedback pattern during power-on attempts.
claims.quote: 1 beep every 5-10 seconds when pressing power button can indicate a short.

procedure: Inspect the board and APU region for liquid metal spills, including under APU seals.
Measure board power rails in diode mode to locate short circuits.
Scan the motherboard with a thermal camera to identify shorted components or thermal abnormalities.
Verify that all required standby and power-on voltage rails are operational.
Check the HDMI encoder IC if power rails are normal and no board shorts are detected.
cautions: Ensure liquid metal has not migrated under the APU surrounding seals or onto board components.
card.caveats: Continuous blue light is a non-specific generic state indicating failure during boot checks; it requires methodical elimination of power rails, liquid metal, encoder IC, and BGA issues.
